newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy firm, but sentiment to worsen - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy firm, but sentiment to worsen - MOF.

text.p: Japan's economy is firm for now, but business sentiment will worsen temporarily after the government implements fiscal tightening measures from April, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Tuesday.
The official said judging from MOF's corporate surveys, the economy was steadily recovering, backed by an improvement in profits and an increase in capital spending.

But he added that the surveys also showed corporate sentiment would worsen in the April-June quarter, hit by the fiscal tightening measures, most notably a planned rise in the national consumption tax.
The Japanese government plans to raise the sales tax to five percent from three percent from April 1.

The ministry's quarterly corporate survey showed that Japanese companies' spending on plant and equipment increased by 10.0 percent in the October-December quarter of 1996 from the same period in the previous year.
It was the first time since the January-March quarter of 1991 that a year-on-year rise exceeded 10 percent, the official told a news conference.
The survey also showed that firms' current profits rose by 15.4 percent in the October-December quarter.
It was the 10th consecutive quarter that profits showed a rise, the official said.
But a separate survey on corporate sentiment showed that Japanese companies' outlook for the April-June period would worsen drastically.
An index representing the percentage of firms expecting business to improve minus those which expect it to worsen showed an overall fall.
While the figure for major firms' outlook for April-June stayed in positive territory, those for medium and smaller firms were in the negative zone, the survey showed.
"It's obvious that the rise in the sales tax is behind the fall in sentiment for the April-June period," the official said.
But he added that the economy was likely to get back on a recovery path in the latter half of the fiscal year.
